### Defenition Info:
For this analysis, I used only games with both home and away teams belonging to a P4 conference.
The "first part" and "second part" of the season were defined as 
    games between weeks 1-8 and weeks 9-15, respectively.
For many teams, their first games aren't accounted for as they have
    light early-season schedules (non-P4 opponents).
Assigning week 8 to the first half of the season helps account for this.

### Best Measures Conclusions:
Based on the following code and metrics tested, the three best offensive metrics for current P4 conference cfb from 2021-2025 regular season are:
    off_success_rate, pass_success_rate, off_ppa.

Alongside these three metrics, I worked with:
    rush_success_rate, pass_ppa, rush_ppa, off_plays, off_explosiveness, pass_explosiveness, and rush_explosiveness.
PPA references predicted points added, 
    Success_rate references a team gaining a specific percentage of their needed yards based on the respective down,
    and Explosiveness references the average expected points added on successful plays

Offensive and passing success rates, alongside offensive ppa were determined to be the three best as they were all
    top 3 for both correlation to win_count and for reliability when comparing their first and second halves of the seasons.
Pass_ppa performed well, too, but was a bit further behind in regards to split reliability.
    Aside from these 4 metrics, no other metric was both reliable and held a relatively strong correlation to 
    both win count and point differential. This was especially the case for off_, rush_, and pass_explosiveness.

```{python}
# Packages required: pandas, numpy, scipy, great_tables, requests

import pandas as pd
import numpy as np
from scipy import stats
from great_tables import GT
import requests
import os

# Set pandas options to display numbers clearly without scientific notation
pd.set_option('display.float_format', lambda x: '%.4f' % x)
```

```{python}
# Verify API key availability
api_key = os.getenv("CFBD_API_KEY", "{YOUR_API_KEY}")

if api_key == "":
    print("Warning: CFBD_API_KEY environment variable not detected.")
else:
    headers = {"Authorization": f"Bearer {api_key}"}
```

```{python}
# P4 regular-season games

seasons = [2021, 2022, 2023, 2024, 2025]
weeks = range(1, 16)
POWER4_CONFERENCES = ["ACC", "Big Ten", "Big 12", "SEC"]

def get_api(url, params):
    resp = requests.get(url, headers=headers, params=params)
    resp.raise_for_status()
    return resp.json()

games_raw = pd.concat(
    [
        pd.DataFrame(
            get_api(
                "https://api.collegefootballdata.com/games",
                {
                    "year": year,
                    "seasonType": "regular",
                    "classification": "fbs",
                },
            )
        )
        for year in seasons
    ],
    ignore_index=True,
)
games_raw = games_raw[
    games_raw["homeConference"].isin(POWER4_CONFERENCES)
    & games_raw["awayConference"].isin(POWER4_CONFERENCES)
].copy()

p4_team_seasons = set(
    pd.concat([
        games_raw[["season", "homeTeam"]].rename(columns={"homeTeam": "team"}),
        games_raw[["season", "awayTeam"]].rename(columns={"awayTeam": "team"}),
    ])
    .drop_duplicates()
    .itertuples(index=False, name=None)
)
print(f"P4 games: {len(games_raw)}")
```

```{python}
# Game-level advanced stats

metric_cols = [
    "off_ppa",
    "off_success_rate",
    "off_explosiveness",
    "off_plays",

    "pass_ppa",
    "pass_success_rate",
    "pass_explosiveness",

    "rush_ppa",
    "rush_success_rate",
    "rush_explosiveness",
]
rows = []
for year in seasons:
    for week in weeks:
        records = get_api(
            "https://api.collegefootballdata.com/stats/game/advanced",
            {
                "year": year,
                "week": week,
                "seasonType": "regular",
            },
        )
        for r in records:
            if (r.get("season"), r.get("team")) not in p4_team_seasons:
                continue
            offense = r.get("offense", {})
            passing = offense.get("passingPlays", {})
            rushing = offense.get("rushingPlays", {})
            rows.append({
                "gameId": r.get("gameId"),
                "season": r.get("season"),
                "week": r.get("week"),
                "team": r.get("team"),
                # overall offense
                "off_ppa": offense.get("ppa"),
                "off_success_rate": offense.get("successRate"),
                "off_explosiveness": offense.get("explosiveness"),
                "off_plays": offense.get("plays"),
                # passing
                "pass_ppa": passing.get("ppa"),
                "pass_success_rate": passing.get("successRate"),
                "pass_explosiveness": passing.get("explosiveness"),
                # rushing
                "rush_ppa": rushing.get("ppa"),
                "rush_success_rate": rushing.get("successRate"),
                "rush_explosiveness": rushing.get("explosiveness"),
            })
game_combined = pd.DataFrame(rows)
game_combined[metric_cols] = game_combined[metric_cols].apply(
    pd.to_numeric,
    errors="coerce"
)
print(f"Game-level rows: {len(game_combined)}")
print("\nRows by season:")
print(game_combined.groupby("season").size())
```

```{python}
# VALIDITY - correlation to wins and point differential
season_metrics = (
    game_combined
    .groupby(["season", "team"])[metric_cols]
    .mean()
    .reset_index()
)
# Wins and point differential
home = games_raw[
    ["season", "homeTeam", "homePoints", "awayPoints"]].rename(columns={"homeTeam": "team"})
home["win"] = (home["homePoints"] > home["awayPoints"]).astype(int)
home["point_diff"] = home["homePoints"] - home["awayPoints"]

away = games_raw[
    ["season", "awayTeam", "homePoints", "awayPoints"]].rename(columns={"awayTeam": "team"})
away["win"] = (away["awayPoints"] > away["homePoints"]).astype(int)
away["point_diff"] = away["awayPoints"] - away["homePoints"]

season_outcomes = (
    pd.concat([
        home[["season", "team", "win", "point_diff"]],
        away[["season", "team", "win", "point_diff"]],
    ])
    .groupby(["season", "team"])
    .agg(
        win_count=("win", "sum"),
        median_point_diff=("point_diff", "median"),
    )
    .reset_index()
)
df_analysis_a = season_metrics.merge(
    season_outcomes,
    on=["season", "team"],
    how="left",
)
# Calculate correlations
corr_wins = (
    df_analysis_a[metric_cols + ["win_count"]]
    .corr()["win_count"]
    .drop("win_count")
)
corr_pd = (
    df_analysis_a[metric_cols + ["median_point_diff"]]
    .corr()["median_point_diff"]
    .drop("median_point_diff")
)
# Combine into one DataFrame
correlation_table = pd.DataFrame({
    "metric": metric_cols,
    "win_count_r": [corr_wins[m] for m in metric_cols],
    "point_diff_r": [corr_pd[m] for m in metric_cols],
})
# Sort by correlation with wins
correlation_table = (
    correlation_table
    .sort_values("win_count_r", ascending=False)
    .reset_index(drop=True)
)

correlation_table
```

```{python}
# RELIABILITY - H1 vs H2 split-half reliability (weeks 1-8 vs weeks 9-15)

game_combined["half"] = np.where(
    game_combined["week"] <= 8,
    "H1",
    "H2"
)
# Make sure all metrics are numeric
game_combined[metric_cols] = game_combined[metric_cols].apply(
    pd.to_numeric,
    errors="coerce"
)
# Average each metric within each half
half_agg = (
    game_combined
    .groupby(["season", "team", "half"])[metric_cols]
    .mean()
    .reset_index()
)
# Pivot H1 and H2
metrics_wide = half_agg.pivot(
    index=["season", "team"],
    columns="half",
    values=metric_cols
)
# Flatten columns
metrics_wide.columns = [
    f"{metric}_{half}"
    for metric, half in metrics_wide.columns
]
metrics_wide = metrics_wide.reset_index()

# Calculate Pearson r, p-value, and R²
corr_data = []
for metric in metric_cols:
    h1 = f"{metric}_H1"
    h2 = f"{metric}_H2"

    valid = metrics_wide[[h1, h2]].dropna()
    if (
        len(valid) >= 2
        and valid[h1].nunique() >= 2
        and valid[h2].nunique() >= 2
    ):
        r, p = stats.pearsonr(
            valid[h1].astype(float),
            valid[h2].astype(float)
        )
    else:
        r = np.nan
        p = np.nan

    corr_data.append({
        "metric": metric,
        "r": r,
        "p_value": p,
        "r_squared": r ** 2 if not np.isnan(r) else np.nan,
    })
correlation_results = (
    pd.DataFrame(corr_data)
    .sort_values("r", ascending=False)
    .reset_index(drop=True)
)
```

```{python}
# Render table
GT(correlation_results).tab_header(
    title="Offensive Metric Split-Half Reliability",
    subtitle="Pearson correlation (r) between Weeks 1–8 (H1) and Weeks 9–15 (H2)"
).cols_label(
    metric="Offensive Metric",
    r="Pearson r",
    p_value="p-value",
    r_squared="R²",
).fmt_number(
    columns=["r", "p_value", "r_squared"],
    decimals=3
)
```
